cqa_tuples.knowledge_point: Definition of process and thread and their relationship
cqa_tuples.target_criteria: FULL (1) only when both definitions and the within-process relationship are explicit. PARTIAL (0.5) when exactly one side is explicitly defined. ABSENT (0) when the answer only discusses shared/private resources or merely implies the relationship without defining either term.
acceptable_variants: process is a program instance, thread is a sub-unit
cqa_tuples.partial_credit_rule: 0.5 marks for defining only one of the two terms.
cqa_tuples.source_rubric_span: 1) Core distinction: a process is an independent running program/program instance with its own resource boundary; a thread is an execution unit within a process. Award FULL (1) only when both definitions and the within-process relationship are explicit. Award PARTIAL (0.5) when exactly one side is explicitly defined. Award ABSENT (0) when the answer only discusses shared/private resources or merely implies the relationship without defining either term; do not infer definitions from parts (a)-(d).
cqa_tuples.source_reference_span: A process is an independent program instance; threads are concurrent execution units within a process.

cqa_tuples.knowledge_point: Resources shared by threads of the same process
cqa_tuples.target_criteria: Identify shared resources such as address space, code, data, heap, or open files.
cqa_tuples.partial_credit_rule: 0.5 marks for identifying at least one shared resource.
cqa_tuples.source_rubric_span: 2) Shared by threads of one process: address space / code+data/heap / open files (any clear statement of shared memory space).
cqa_tuples.source_reference_span: Threads in the same process typically share the process address space: code, data/heap, and open OS resources such as file descriptors

cqa_tuples.target_criteria: Identify per-thread private resources such as stack, registers, or program counter.
cqa_tuples.partial_credit_rule: 0.5 marks for identifying at least one private resource.
cqa_tuples.source_rubric_span: 3) Per-thread private: stack and/or registers/PC/thread context.
cqa_tuples.source_reference_span: Each thread has its own stack, register context / program counter, and thread-local scheduling state (thread ID).

cqa_tuples.target_criteria: Identify one clear advantage such as lighter weight, faster creation/switching, or easy shared-memory communication.
cqa_tuples.partial_credit_rule: 0.5 marks for a partially correct or vague advantage.
cqa_tuples.source_rubric_span: 4) Advantage: lighter weight, faster create/switch, easy shared-memory communication (any one clear advantage).
cqa_tuples.source_reference_span: Advantage: cheaper context switch / shared memory communication is easy — creating threads and sharing data is lighter than creating processes and using IPC.

cqa_tuples.target_criteria: Identify one clear risk such as weaker isolation, shared-memory corruption, or synchronization requirements.
cqa_tuples.partial_credit_rule: 0.5 marks for a partially correct or vague risk.
cqa_tuples.source_rubric_span: 5) Disadvantage: weaker isolation / shared-memory bugs / need locks; process isolation is safer (any one clear risk).
cqa_tuples.source_reference_span: Disadvantage: one buggy thread can corrupt shared memory and crash the whole process; also needs synchronization (races). Separate processes give stronger isolation.
